sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very closely related to H. nidicola, from which it differs in the distinctly broader pronotum (Fig. 274). Tibial spurs 3:2:2. Measurements (mm): length with wings 11.25—12.25; length without wings 5.75—6.00; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.13; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.55; head width 0.97—1.08; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.27; ocellus length 0.09; pronotum length 0.73—0.80; pronotum width 1.02—1.21; fore wing length 8.90—8.96; fore wing width 2.70.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Differs from H. nidicola as follows: the two lobes of the postclypeus are shorter and more rounded, the labrum is distinctly narrower and more pointed, and the middle of the anterior dorsal margin of the head is more raised (Fig. 275). Tibial spurs 3:2:2. Measurements (mm): body length 4.20—5.50; head length including mandibles 1.85—2.20; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.10—1.21; head width 0.82—0.93; pronotum length 0.33—0.40; pronotum width 0.71—0.80.

note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Hill (1942); the original is in English. The original combination is Ahamitermes hillii Nicholls, 1929, and the heading reads Hamitermes (Ahamitermes) hilli (Nicholls) (OCRed as Tiilli). Measurements in mm. Distribution: Western Australia, Kalgoorlie (type locality), Karramindie, Greenbushes, Toodyay, Mt. Barker. The original records the species from only five or six series of specimens, all taken from the clay outer walls of nests of Coptotermes (probably C. acinaciformis and C. raffrayi); the alate form is known from only two series (collected on 3/20 and 4/26). The original considers this species very probably a geographical race of H. nidicola. Type material: an alate lectotype, with soldier and worker lectomorphotypes, deposited in C.S.I.R. OCR problem: the soldier body length is printed "4.20 5-50" without the connector and is read as 4.20—5.50.
